info.title: Presaleee Backend API
info.description: HTTP surface of the Presaleee presale platform, documented from the Express  routers in `src/presentation/routes/` (77 registered handlers plus the  `GET /health` system probe). Every statement here mirrors the code: request  fields, defaults, limits, enums, status codes and role guards.  Success: `{ "success": true, "data": <resource>, "meta"?: {...} }`.  Failure: `{ "success": false, "error": "<message>", "statusCode": <n> }`  (`src/presentation/middlewares/errorHandler.ts:20-44`). An uncaught  non-domain error answers `500` with `error: "Internal server error occurred."`  and is never leaked verbatim.  `ValidationError` 400, `UnauthorizedError` 401, `AppError` 403,  `NotFoundError` 404 (also used for another tenant's resource, so a  cross-tenant id is indistinguishable from a missing one),  `ConflictError` 409, `ExternalServiceError` 502. body-parser adds  `400` malformed JSON, `413` payload over 2 MB (`src/index.ts:21`) and  `415` unsupported encoding.  Staff calls present a 15-minute HS256 access token, either as  `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` (wins when both are sent) or as the  `presaleee_access` cookie. Claims are `sub`, `email`, `organizationId`  (nullable), `role` (defaults `VIEWER`) (`src/presentation/middlewares/requireAuth.ts:22-51`).  A refresh token is only ever carried by the `presaleee_refresh` cookie and  is never serialized into a body.  Two guards are layered on top of `requireAuth`: `requireOrganization`  answers `403 An organization is required for this operation.` when the  token has no `organizationId`, and `requireRole(...)` answers  `403 This operation requires one of the following roles: <roles>.`  (`src/presentation/middlewares/requireRole.ts:14-16`).  The client portal is a separate security scheme: an opaque 43-character  base64url token issued by `POST /api/v1/portal/sessions`, presented as  `Authorization: Bearer <portalToken>`. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored, and  the session row is checked against `proposal_id`, `revoked_at IS NULL`,  `expires_at > NOW()` and proposal status in `SENT_TO_CLIENT`/`ACCEPTED`  (`src/presentation/routes/portalRoutes.ts:17-31`).  All six cookie-writing auth routes and `POST /auth/register` compare the  `Origin` header against `FRONTEND_URL`: absent origin passes, unparsable  origin is `400 Invalid request origin.`, mismatched origin is  `403 Request origin is not allowed.` (`src/presentation/controllers/AuthController.ts:56-70`).  Six operations call the external Python service  `${AI_SERVICE_URL}/api/v1/generate` (default `http://localhost:8000`) and  answer `502` when it is unreachable: `POST /leads/intake/analyze`,  `POST /leads/{id}/qualifications`, `POST /meetings/{meetingId}/analyze`,  `POST /proposals/{id}/generate`, `POST /proposals/{id}/sheets/{sheetName}/generate`,  `POST /proposals/{id}/sections/{sectionName}/regenerate`,  `POST /portal/proposals/{proposalId}/questions`,  `POST /knowledge/ask`, `POST /rag/generate-proposal`.  Retrieval and ingest use the Gemini embedding gateway directly  (`gemini-embedding-001`, 768 dimensions) and only fail with `502` if that  call fails.  Collection paths are written without a trailing slash (`/api/v1/proposals`);  the routers register them as `router.post('/')` under a mount, so Express  accepts both forms. A request body larger than 2 MB is answered `413`, and an  unsupported `Content-Encoding` `415` - both apply to every operation that  accepts a body and are not repeated per operation. `GET` exports are the only  operations whose success body is binary rather than the JSON envelope.  Regenerate and re-check this file with `npm run docs:openapi`, which fails if a  route is registered in `src/presentation/routes/` but missing here.

servers.description: Isolated e2e instance used by the API test suites

get.summary: Service liveness probe
get.description: Registered directly on the Express app before the `/api/v1` router, so  it is not behind auth and does not use the response envelope  (`src/index.ts:24-31`).

post.summary: Register a user and create its organization
post.description: Self-service sign-up. The caller always becomes `ADMIN` of a brand-new  organization, and the response also carries that organization. Only the  access cookie is set here; the refresh token is returned in the body so  a non-browser client can store it. The identity is taken from the  verified user row, never from the request body, and `role`/`status` are  not accepted as input.

post.summary: Start a session with email and password
post.description: Sets both httpOnly cookies (`presaleee_access` for 15 minutes,  `presaleee_refresh` for 30 days) and returns only the user object. A  wrong password, an unknown email and a non-`ACTIVE` account all answer  the same `401 Invalid email or password.` so the response cannot be used  to enumerate accounts. There is no rate limiting on this route.

post.summary: Rotate the session from the refresh cookie
post.description: Reads `presaleee_refresh` (32-256 characters) - there is no request  body and a token passed in the body is ignored. The stored token is  hashed and compared, the old session row is revoked and a new pair is  issued (rotation), so replaying a used refresh token gives `401`. On any  failure both cookies are cleared.

post.summary: Revoke the refresh session and clear the cookies
post.description: Revokes the session behind `presaleee_refresh` and clears both cookies.  An absent or unknown refresh token is a silent no-op, so logout is  idempotent and always answers `200`. Note the accepted limitation - the  15-minute access token stays valid until it expires.

get.summary: Read the authenticated identity
get.description: Resolves `sub` from the token to a fresh user row, so a deactivated  account answers `401 User is not active.` even while its token is still  valid.

post.summary: Request a password reset token
post.description: Always answers `200` with the same neutral message, for an unknown or  inactive email too. Outside `NODE_ENV=production` the response also  carries `resetToken` and `resetUrl` so the flow is testable without mail  delivery; in production those two fields are absent.

200.description: Reset requested. Token exposed only outside production.

post.summary: Consume a reset token and set a new password
post.description: The token must be 32-256 characters and the password must pass the  12-128 character policy, which is validated before the token is  consumed so a weak password does not burn a valid token. A successful  reset invalidates the old password, every live refresh session and both  cookies; a used, expired or unknown token answers  `409 Password reset token is invalid, expired, or already used.`

get.summary: List the organizations the caller can join
get.description: The only users route that tolerates a token without `organizationId`  (used right after sign-up). Returns a plain array, not a page, so  `meta.total` is the array length rather than a database count.

patch.summary: Update own profile or change own password
patch.description: At least one editable field is required. Supplying `password` also  requires `currentPassword`, which is verified against the stored hash  (`401 Current password is incorrect.`) and, on success, revokes every  refresh session so other devices are signed out. `avatarUrl` accepts  `null` or an empty string to clear it. Role and status cannot be changed  here.

passwordChanged.description: True only when a new password was accepted.

get.summary: List the staff directory of the caller organization
get.description: `requireAuth` only - every role can read the directory. Results are  scoped to the token's organization unless an `ADMIN` adds  `allOrganizations=true`, which is rejected with `403` for any other role  because it widens the tenant filter. `search` matches `full_name` or  `email` with ILIKE.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Note the default here is 50, not 20.

parameters.name: allOrganizations
parameters.description: Literal `true` to span organizations. ADMIN only.

post.summary: Invite or create a member in the caller organization
post.description: Guarded by `requireRole(ADMIN, PRESALE_LEAD)`. The new account is bound  to the caller's organization, so `organizationId` is never accepted from  the body. An unknown role is a `400`, a taken email a `409`.

201.description: Member created, with `Location: /api/v1/users/{id}`. No `organizationName`  on this row.

get.summary: Read one member of the caller organization
get.description: Any authenticated role. A row from another tenant answers `404`, not  `403`. A path segment that is not a UUID answers `400`.

patch.summary: Change a member's name, role or status
patch.description: Guarded by `requireRole(ADMIN, PRESALE_LEAD)`. Changing your own `role`  or `status` through this route is rejected with `400` - use  `PATCH /users/me` semantics for that, so an administrator cannot lock  themselves out by accident. Demoting or deactivating the last active  `ADMIN` answers `409 The organization must keep at least one active ADMIN.`;  setting `status=DEACTIVATED` revokes that user's refresh sessions.

get.summary: List the client directory
get.description: Read access for every role in the organization. Ordered  `updated_at DESC, created_at DESC`. `search` matches company name,  contact person or contact email.

parameters.name: industry
parameters.description: Exact match against the industry taxonomy. These are display labels, not codes.

post.summary: Register a client company
post.description: Guarded by `requireRole(ADMIN, PRESALE_LEAD)`. The client is bound to the  caller's organization; `organizationId` in the body is ignored. The  unique constraint is on the company name per organization, so a  duplicate answers `409`. `contactEmail` is stored as free text - it is  not format-validated, unlike the portal's client email.

201.description: Client created; the response also carries a `Location` header pointing at the new resource.

get.summary: Read one client

patch.description: Guarded by `requireRole(ADMIN, PRESALE_LEAD)`. Every field is optional  but at least one must be present, otherwise `400 At least one editable  field is required.`. A nullable field set to `null` is stored as NULL  except `companyName` and `country`, which cannot be emptied.

delete.summary: Delete a client that has no leads
delete.description: Guarded by `requireRole(ADMIN, PRESALE_LEAD)`. Refused while leads still  reference the client - `409 Reassign the N lead(s) to another client  before deleting.` - because the FK is `ON DELETE RESTRICT` and losing the  company link silently would corrupt the pipeline.

get.summary: List the leads attached to a client
get.description: Same projection as `GET /leads` - `rawRfpContent` and `bantDetails` are  stripped. The client is checked first, so an unknown client gives  `404 Client not found.` rather than an empty list.

get.summary: List the organization's rate cards
get.description: Ordered `level DESC, role_name ASC`. Inactive cards are hidden unless  `includeInactive=true`, because the pricing calculator must not pick a  retired rate.

parameters.name: roleName
parameters.description: ILIKE substring match on the role name.

parameters.name: includeInactive
parameters.description: Only the literal `true` or `false` is accepted.

post.summary: Create a rate card for a role and level
post.description: Guarded by `requireRole(ADMIN, PRESALE_LEAD)`. At least one of  `hourlyRateUsd`, `dailyRateUsd`, `monthlyRateUsd` must be above zero,  otherwise the card could never price anything - that is a `400`. Unique  per (roleName, level, currency), so a duplicate answers `409`.

201.description: Rate card created; the response also carries a `Location` header pointing at the new resource.

post.summary: Price a bill of materials against the rate cards
post.description: Pure arithmetic, no LLM: the AI proposes effort, this endpoint turns it  into money. Read access only (`requireAuth` + `requireOrganization`), so  any role can cost a quotation. Each line resolves its monthly rate as  explicit monthly, else daily x 21 billable days, else hourly x 8 x 21,  and reports which route was taken in `rateSource`. An override is only  honoured when it is positive, which is what keeps a hand-typed value  from silently replacing a real rate. Mix two currencies in one call and  the whole request is rejected. With `proposalId` (and `apply` left out or  true) the total is written to the proposal and the updated proposal is  returned; otherwise `proposal` is `null`.

200.description: Calculated pricing, plus the proposal when applied.

400.description: One of `NO_LINES`, `TOO_MANY_LINES`, `INVALID_EFFORT`, `INVALID_RATE`,  `UNKNOWN_ROLE` (with the available roles listed) or `MIXED_CURRENCY`,  or `apply=true` without a `proposalId`.

404.description: `proposalId` does not belong to the caller's organization.

get.summary: Read one rate card

patch.summary: Edit or deactivate a rate card
patch.description: Guarded by `requireRole(ADMIN, PRESALE_LEAD)`. The zero-rate guardrail is  re-checked against the merged row, so you cannot deactivate every rate at  once. When `hourlyRateUsd` or `dailyRateUsd` changes and no monthly rate  is set, `monthlyRateUsd` is re-derived (daily x 21, else hourly x 8 x 21)  so the card stays internally consistent.

delete.description: Guarded by `requireRole(ADMIN, PRESALE_LEAD)`. Nothing stops you from  deleting the last card for a role - pricing then fails with  `UNKNOWN_ROLE` instead of `409` here.

post.summary: Turn raw RFP text into an unsaved lead draft
post.description: Calls the Python LLM service to extract project metadata and list what  the RFP left open. Nothing is written to the database - the response  carries `meta.persisted=false` and a draft whose `id`, `organizationId`,  `status` and timestamps are all `null`, ready for a human to review  before `POST /leads`. `source` defaults to `MANUAL`. A 50,000-character  RFP is the maximum, and a service outage is a `502`, not a partial draft.

value.rawRfpContent: We need a customer-facing pricing calculator for our  logistics platform by Q4, SAP integration required, budget  around 120000 USD.

get.summary: List leads in the pipeline
get.description: Every role can read. `search` matches title OR the raw RFP content with  ILIKE, so it is the only way to find a phrase typed into the intake  text. The list projection omits `rawRfpContent` and `bantDetails`.

parameters.name: assignedTo
parameters.description: Filter by owning user. Must be a UUID.

post.summary: Persist a lead
post.description: `organizationId` and `createdBy` come from the token, not the body. A new  lead always starts at `status=NEW`; reaching any other status requires  `PATCH /leads/{id}/status`. `clientId` and `assignedTo` are validated as  UUIDs only - there is no existence check, so a dangling reference is  accepted here and surfaces later as a missing client name.

value.title: Logistics pricing calculator
value.rawRfpContent: Customer wants a quoting tool integrated with SAP.

201.description: Lead created with `Location: /api/v1/leads/{id}`. Full row including  `rawRfpContent`.

get.summary: Read one lead including its RFP text

patch.summary: Edit lead fields, but not its status
patch.description: At least one field is required. Sending `status` here is refused with  `400` and a pointer to `PATCH /leads/{id}/status`, because the status  machine and its audit trail must not be bypassed by a generic edit.

delete.description: There is no role guard and no confirmation. Note the accepted side  effect: `proposals.lead_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so a proposal that  was generated from this lead survives and silently loses its pipeline  link (and therefore disappears from the dashboard stages).

patch.summary: Move a lead along the pipeline
patch.description: The only legal way to change a lead status. Requests that name the  current status are a no-op and return the lead unchanged. `APPROVED`  additionally requires a stored BANT score - the update is written with a  `bant_score IS NOT NULL` guard, so a race or a missing qualification  answers `409 Lead status changed or the required qualification is  missing.` rather than approving an unqualified lead. Every transition  writes a `LEAD_STATUS_CHANGED` audit row.

409.description: Illegal transition, or approval without a qualification.

example.error: Lead cannot transition from QUALIFYING to WON.

post.summary: Score the lead with BANT and persist the result
post.description: No request body is read. The LLM is asked for a BANT breakdown, the  answer is validated in code (each criterion 0-25, the total must equal  the sum of the four criteria, the recommendation must be one of  `QUALIFY`/`REVIEW`/`DISQUALIFY`) and then written to the lead together  with `status=QUALIFIED`. Invalid AI output is a `409` - the lead is left  untouched - and an unreachable service is a `502`.

get.summary: Read the stored BANT result
get.description: Returns `lead.bantDetails` as saved. A lead that has never been  qualified answers `404 Lead has no qualification result.` rather than an  empty object, so the UI cannot render a score of zero.

200.description: The last qualification written for this lead.

get.summary: List discovery meetings attached to a lead
get.description: Ordered `meeting_date DESC, created_at DESC`. `meta.total` is the length  of the returned array - this collection is not paginated.

post.summary: Schedule a discovery meeting for a lead
post.description: `meetingDate` defaults to the moment of the call and must parse as a  date if supplied. Attendee emails are trimmed before validation, so a  trailing space is accepted; a malformed address is `400`. New meetings  start `OPEN`, which is the only status in which a transcript can be  written.

201.description: Meeting created; the response also carries a `Location` header pointing at the new resource.

post.summary: Create the proposal that belongs to a qualified lead
post.description: The only way to link a proposal to a lead - `leadId` is deliberately not  accepted from any request body elsewhere. The lead must be  `QUALIFIED`, `APPROVED` or `PROPOSAL_DRAFTING`, otherwise `409`. The new  proposal starts as `DRAFT`, `v1.0`, `currency=USD`, with all ten  standard sheets, and the Overview plus Scope of Work sheets are  pre-filled from the lead's extracted metadata.

title.description: Defaults to the lead title when omitted or empty.

201.description: Proposal created; the response also carries a `Location` header pointing at the new resource.

409.description: The lead is not in a state that allows proposal creation.

example.error: Lead must be qualified or approved before proposal creation.

get.summary: Read one discovery meeting
get.description: The full meeting object, including the raw transcript and the analysis.  `analysis` is `{}` until `POST /meetings/{meetingId}/analyze` succeeds,  and the structured `decisions`, `actionItems`, `openQuestions` and  `gapAnalysis` columns stay empty arrays in the same situation.

post.summary: Store or extend the meeting transcript
post.description: `transcript` and `content` are accepted as aliases for the same string  (max 500,000 characters). `append=true` concatenates to what is already  stored with a blank line between, otherwise the transcript is replaced.  Writing a transcript clears the previous analysis, because notes and  conclusions would otherwise disagree. Only allowed while the meeting is  `OPEN` - a `LOCKED` or `INSPECTED` meeting answers  `409 Transcript can only be changed while the meeting is OPEN.`

post.summary: Summarize the transcript with the AI service
post.description: No body. Requires a non-empty transcript (`409 Add a transcript before  analyzing the meeting.`). The answer is validated field by field and then  written into the meeting - clean notes, decisions, action items, open  questions, gap analysis, `analyzedAt` - and the status is forced to  `INSPECTED`. It also appends a `discoveryInsights` entry to the parent  lead's `extractedMetadata`, so the proposal generator can read the  conclusions.

200.description: Meeting analysed and locked in as INSPECTED.

409.description: No transcript, unusable AI output, or a concurrent update.

patch.summary: Lock, reopen or mark a meeting inspected
patch.description: Legal moves are OPEN to LOCKED, LOCKED to OPEN and INSPECTED to OPEN.  `INSPECTED` cannot be requested directly - it is set by a successful  analysis, which is why an invalid transition answers  `409 INSPECTED status is set by successful AI analysis; reopen a meeting  by changing it to OPEN.`

get.summary: List proposals
get.description: The list projection has no `sheets` array - fetch one proposal to read  its content. `search` matches the title with ILIKE only.

post.summary: Create an empty proposal
post.description: Creates the ten standard sheets unless `initialSheets` is supplied.  `leadId` is read from neither the body nor the query - use  `POST /leads/{leadId}/proposals` to attach a proposal to the pipeline.  When `totalCost` or `estimatedTimelineWeeks` is omitted it is seeded from  the Pricing `grandTotal` and Timeline `totalWeeks` of the sheets that were  just written. Status is always `DRAFT`.

201.description: Proposal created; the response also carries a `Location` header pointing at the new resource.

get.summary: Read a proposal with every sheet
get.description: `sheets` is ordered by `sheetOrder`. `totalCost` and  `estimatedTimelineWeeks` are kept in sync with the Pricing and Timeline  sheets on every sheet write, so they are the values to display.

patch.summary: Edit proposal metadata, or move its status
patch.description: Metadata and status cannot be changed in the same request (`400`), and  metadata edits are refused once the proposal leaves `DRAFT`  (`409 Only a DRAFT proposal can be edited.`) - an approved document must  not change underneath a client. Transitions to `APPROVED`,  `REJECTED`, `SENT_TO_CLIENT` or `ACCEPTED` require `ADMIN` or  `PRESALE_LEAD`; other moves are open to every role, which is the recorded  RBAC gap for this route. The legal map is  DRAFT to IN_REVIEW/REJECTED, IN_REVIEW to DRAFT/APPROVED/REJECTED,  APPROVED to IN_REVIEW/SENT_TO_CLIENT/REJECTED, SENT_TO_CLIENT to  ACCEPTED/REJECTED, REJECTED to DRAFT, and ACCEPTED is terminal.

200.description: Proposal updated. The response has no `sheets` array.

delete.description: Hard delete with no role guard and no status precondition - a proposal  already sent to a client can be removed. Portal sessions and materials  cascade with it. Nothing is written to the audit ledger.

put.description: The whole `sheetData` object is replaced, so the caller must send the  complete sheet - a partial payload deletes the rest. Only the DRAFT  status is editable; an unknown sheet name is `400`. Two keys are  validated because the proposal totals are derived from them:  `Pricing & Quotation.grandTotal` must be a non-negative finite number and  `Timeline & Milestones.totalWeeks` a positive integer. `aiGenerated` is  forced to `false` by the controller, so a human edit always wins over the  "AI wrote this" marker. No role guard: any authenticated role, VIEWER  included, can rewrite a sheet.

sheetData.description: Free-form object; its keys depend on the sheet (see the  `sheetData` defaults in the `ProposalSheet` schema).

200.description: The updated sheet only (not the proposal). `totalCost` and  `estimatedTimelineWeeks` on the parent proposal are re-synced.

post.summary: Generate proposal sheets with AI and RAG grounding
post.description: Runs one LLM call per requested sheet (all ten when `sheetNames` is  omitted), each grounded on the five closest knowledge chunks. Only a  DRAFT proposal can be generated (`409`). Numeric sheets are checked after  generation - an AI `grandTotal` or `totalWeeks` that fails validation  aborts with `409` rather than storing a broken quotation. Sources are  returned for citation display.

post.summary: Regenerate a single sheet
post.description: Identical to `POST /proposals/{id}/generate` with `sheetNames` pinned to  the path segment, which must name a standard sheet. The whole sheet is  overwritten, `aiGenerated` becomes `true`.

instructions.description: Free-text steering appended to the prompt.

post.summary: Regenerate the section named in the path
post.description: Same pipeline as the per-sheet route - the path segment is matched against  the ten standard sheet names after `decodeURIComponent`, so a name like  `Risk%20Management%20(RAID)` works and an unknown one is a `400`.

parameters.name: sectionName
parameters.description: Sheet name, URL-encoded when it contains spaces or brackets.

post.summary: Move a DRAFT proposal to IN_REVIEW
post.description: A convenience transition with no body. It is the one status move that no  role can perform on a non-DRAFT proposal - `409 Only a DRAFT proposal can  be submitted for review.` - and a concurrent status change also answers  `409`. Writes a `PROPOSAL_STATUS_CHANGED` audit row.

get.summary: Download the proposal as PDF
get.description: Rendered locally from the stored sheets, at any status. The body is the  binary PDF, so a JSON error envelope can still arrive with  `Content-Type: application/json` when the proposal is missing. Filename is  `{sanitizedTitle}_Proposal_{version}.pdf` where the title keeps only  `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`.

get.summary: Download the proposal as an xlsx workbook
get.description: One worksheet per sheet plus the pricing detail. Known finding: the  Pricing tab hard-codes "VAT 10%" instead of the stored `taxPercentage`,  and the Team tab prints stored money numbers rather than recomputing rate  times man-months, so a workbook can disagree with the API totals.

get.summary: List every material of a proposal, shared or not
get.description: Staff-side list. No role guard, so a VIEWER sees the whole material set  including rows with `isShared=false`. `meta.total` is the array length;  the collection is not paginated.

post.summary: Attach a material link to a proposal
post.description: Restricted to `PORTAL_MANAGER_ROLES` (`ADMIN`, `PRESALE_LEAD`,  `SALES_REP`, `SOLUTION_ARCHITECT`, and `PRESALE_CONSULTANT` which is not  in `USER_ROLES`). There is no upload - `fileUrl` must be an `https://`  URL, so the file itself lives elsewhere. The proposal must already be  `APPROVED`, `SENT_TO_CLIENT` or `ACCEPTED`, otherwise `404` rather than  `409`. `isShared` defaults to `false`, and the created row is answered  without `isShared`/`createdBy`, so the caller cannot read back what it  just set.

404.description: Proposal not found, or not yet eligible for portal materials.

delete.description: `PORTAL_MANAGER_ROLES` only. A material of another proposal, or of  another tenant, is `404 Portal material not found.`; the pair of ids is  matched together.

get.summary: List the portal sessions issued for a proposal
get.description: Shows revoked sessions too, with `revokedAt`, and a `commentCount` so the  UI can badge activity. No role guard - a VIEWER can read every client  email and name on this list; this is a recorded finding. Token material  (the hash) is never serialized.

post.summary: Issue a client portal link
post.description: Restricted to `PORTAL_MANAGER_ROLES`. The proposal must be `APPROVED`,  `SENT_TO_CLIENT` or `ACCEPTED`; sharing an `APPROVED` one also flips it to  `SENT_TO_CLIENT` in the same transaction, and only `ADMIN`/`PRESALE_LEAD`  may do that. The plaintext `accessToken` (43-character base64url) is  returned exactly once - only its SHA-256 hash is stored - so this response  cannot be reconstructed later. `expiresInHours` defaults to 168 (7 days)  and caps at 720 (30 days). `clientEmail` is lower-cased and must be a valid  address, unlike the client directory's free-text contact email.

201.description: Session created, with the one-time token.

409.description: The proposal is not in a shareable status.

example.error: Only an approved proposal can be shared with a client.

delete.description: `PORTAL_MANAGER_ROLES` only. Soft revoke - the row keeps its audit value  with `revoked_at` set, and the token stops working immediately, including  mid-conversation. An already-revoked or unknown session answers `404`, which  makes a second revoke a `404` rather than an idempotent `204`.

get.summary: Client view of the shared proposal
get.description: Authenticated by the portal token, not by a staff account. The projection  hides `organizationId`, `leadId`, `createdBy` and the sheet ids, but every  one of the ten sheets is included - internal ones such as  `Team & Rate Cards` and `Pricing & Quotation` too, which is a recorded  finding. `last_accessed_at` is bumped on each successful call. The proposal  must be `SENT_TO_CLIENT` or `ACCEPTED`, otherwise `404 Shared proposal  not found.`

404.description: Session is bound to a different, or no longer shared, proposal.

post.summary: Ask a question about the shared proposal
post.description: Answers from the proposal's own sheets: every sheet contributes one  citation whose `excerpt` is the first 1800 characters of its JSON, so the  reply is grounded in what the client was shown. The question is capped at  5000 characters and the LLM call failing is a `502`.

200.description: Answer plus one citation per sheet.

get.summary: Read the feedback thread of the shared proposal
get.description: The most recent 500 comments, oldest first. Comments are flat - there is no  parent/thread field in the schema. A commenter can see every comment on the  proposal, including other people from the same organization.

post.summary: Leave feedback on the shared proposal
post.description: `authorEmail` always comes from the session, never from the body, so a  client cannot forge another sender. `authorName` defaults to the session's  client name or email. Returns `201` with the stored row, and `404` when the  session was revoked or the proposal left the shared states mid-conversation.

get.summary: List the materials marked as shared
get.description: Filtered to `is_shared = TRUE`, unlike the staff list on the sibling  `/proposals/{proposalId}/portal-materials` route which returns everything.

get.summary: Download the shared proposal as PDF
get.description: The same renderer the staff export uses, after re-checking that the  proposal is still shared. `Content-Type: application/pdf` with an  attachment disposition.

get.summary: List indexed knowledge documents
get.description: `search` matches the title only - full-text search over chunk content is  `POST /rag/search`. There is no role guard, so a VIEWER can read the whole  vault listing.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Free text, max 100 characters. There is no closed enum; `GENERAL` is  the value written when ingest omits it.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Same free-text filter, applied to the domain column.

post.summary: Index a document into the vault
post.description: Splits `content` into roughly 400-word windows with 50-word overlap, asks  the Gemini embedding gateway for a 768-dimension vector per chunk and  writes them transactionally - if embedding fails, no document row is left  behind. `content` is chunked and discarded: the `knowledge_docs` table has  no content column, so the document body only survives inside  `document_chunks`, and `GET /knowledge/documents/{id}` cannot echo it back.  Identical text ingested twice is embedded and stored twice - there is no  dedupe. No role guard on this route.

value.title: Payment gateway integration guide
value.content: Our standard integration covers 3DS2, webhooks and  reconciliation. Each payment attempt emits an event to the  merchant queue...

get.summary: Read a document's metadata
get.description: Metadata only - chunk content lives in `document_chunks` and is reachable  through `POST /rag/search`. A document of another organization is `404`.

delete.summary: Delete a document and its chunks
delete.description: Cascades to `document_chunks`, so retrieval stops returning its text  immediately. No role guard - a VIEWER can empty the vault, which is a  recorded finding.

post.summary: Ask the vault a grounded question
post.description: Hybrid retrieval first (Gemini embedding of the question plus PostgreSQL  `hybrid_search_chunks`), then the Python service writes the answer from  those excerpts. Numbered `[1]`-style citations reference the chunks that  were actually used, so a wrong answer is traceable. `topK` is 1-10,  default 5. Needs the LLM service; without it the call is a `502` even  though retrieval itself succeeded.

post.summary: Hybrid full-text plus vector search
post.description: Runs PostgreSQL `hybrid_search_chunks` with equal full-text and semantic  weights and RRF `k=60`, scoped to the caller's organization and optionally  one `domain`. Deterministic and cheap enough to be the read model for the  other AI routes. `topK` here is 1-20, default 3. Known finding: the SQL  never selects `chunk_index`, so every hit reports `chunkIndex` 0 and  `semanticRank`/`ftsRank` are the only ordering signals that mean anything.

post.summary: Index a document (RAG-flavoured alias)
post.description: The same use case as `POST /knowledge/documents` - identical validation,  chunking and embedding - but the response adds a human-readable `message`.  Both write to the same tables, so the two routes are interchangeable.

post.summary: Draft a proposal overview from an RFP
post.description: The legacy single-shot generator: retrieve three chunks, ask the model for  an overview, return both. It does not create a `proposals` row - use  `POST /proposals` plus `POST /proposals/{id}/generate` for a persisted  document. Retrieval is fixed at topK 3 and `maxTokens` is 1-8000.

200.description: Overview text plus the sources it came from.

get.summary: Pipeline KPIs, stage counts and the active-lead panel
get.description: Aggregates computed live from `leads` and `proposals` for the caller's  organization. `pipeline` always contains all nine stages in order, each  with its lead count and its per-currency estimated value (REJECTED  proposals excluded from the money). `kpis.activeLeads` counts anything not  WON/LOST/REJECTED while `qualifiedLeads` counts  QUALIFIED/PROPOSAL_DRAFTING/APPROVED. The `activeLeads` panel is capped by  `leadLimit` (default 8, 1-50). No role guard, so a VIEWER reads the whole  revenue pipeline. A `?organizationId` in the query is ignored - the scope  always comes from the token.

parameters.name: leadLimit
parameters.description: Size of the active-lead panel. An empty value means "not provided" and  falls back to the default, like every other list endpoint.

get.summary: Recent active leads for a widget
get.description: Excludes WON, LOST and REJECTED. `clientName` is joined server-side and the  RFP text is never included. `meta.total` is the number of rows returned,  not the tenant-wide count, so a widget cannot tell that more rows sit  behind `limit`.

get.summary: Recent activity feed
get.description: Synthesized from `leads.created_at/updated_at` and  `proposals.created_at/updated_at` - NOT from `audit_logs`. Each entity can  contribute at most two rows (`<uuid>:created` and `<uuid>:updated`), an  `:updated` row only exists when `updated_at` is more than one second after  creation, and a later edit overwrites the earlier one, so this feed cannot  reconcile with G14 and never shows sheet writes, pricing applies, portal  sessions or deletes.

get.summary: Read the organization's activity ledger
get.description: `requireRole(ADMIN, PRESALE_LEAD)`; every other role gets `403` naming the  allowed roles. Newest first, scoped to the token's organization, and the  ledger itself has no write, update or delete route. `actorName` is resolved  by a LEFT JOIN on `users`, so a deleted actor yields `null` rather than  disappearing. `ip_address` is stored but never serialized, and a payload is  returned as an object (a non-object column value becomes `{}`).  Two limitations to know before building a security view on this: no code  path ever writes `resultStatus=FAILED`, so filtering on it always returns  nothing, and `from`/`to` are validated individually but never compared -  `from` after `to` is a silent empty page.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Exact match, max 100 characters. Observed values include  `USER_REGISTERED`, `USER_CREATED`, `CLIENT_CREATED`, `LEAD_CREATED`,  `LEAD_UPDATED`, `LEAD_STATUS_CHANGED`, `PROPOSAL_STATUS_CHANGED`,  `RATE_CARD_CREATED`, `PRICING_APPLIED`, `PORTAL_SESSION_CREATED`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Parsed with `Date.parse`, so short forms such as `2020` or `0` are  accepted and silently normalized rather than rejected. Applied as  `created_at >= from`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Default 50 and maximum 200 - wider than the other lists.

bearerAccess.description: Staff access token, HS256, 900 second lifetime. `Bearer` takes  precedence when both this header and the cookie are present.

accessCookie.name: presaleee_access
accessCookie.description: The same access token as an httpOnly cookie with `path=/api/v1/auth`,  `sameSite` from `AUTH_COOKIE_SAME_SITE` and `secure` from  `AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE`.

portalBearer.description: Client portal token returned once by `POST /api/v1/portal/sessions`  (`accessToken`). Not a JWT; only its SHA-256 hash is stored.

UuidPathId.name: id
UuidPathId.description: Resource id. Must be a valid UUID (version 1-8 variant checked); a  numeric, boolean or malformed value is rejected as `400` before any query  runs.

SheetNamePath.name: sheetName
SheetNamePath.description: One of the ten standard sheet names. Percent-encode the spaces, for  example `Pricing%20%26%20Quotation`; the value is URI-decoded before it is  matched.

DashboardLimitParam.name: limit
DashboardLimitParam.description: Rows for this widget. Default 20, maximum 100; `0`, `101` and non-integers  are `400` and the message names this parameter.

OriginHeader.name: Origin
OriginHeader.description: Browser origin. Checked against `FRONTEND_URL` by the cookie-writing  auth routes; a non-browser caller may omit it.

BadRequest.description: `ValidationError` - unparsable JSON, oversized field, unknown enum  value, malformed UUID, empty patch, invalid pagination or limit.

example.error: title must be a string of at most 255 characters.

Unauthorized.description: `UnauthorizedError` - no token, expired or badly signed token, a portal  session that is revoked/expired, or a credential check that failed.

Forbidden.description: `AppError` 403 - the token role is not in the route's allow-list, the  token carries no `organizationId`, or the `Origin` does not match  `FRONTEND_URL`.

example.error: This operation requires one of the following roles: ADMIN, PRESALE_LEAD.

NotFound.description: `NotFoundError` - the id is unknown to the caller's organization. A row  owned by another tenant also answers `404`, never `403`, so tenant  existence is not leaked.

Conflict.description: `ConflictError` - a unique constraint, a state-machine violation, an  optimistic-locking race, or a missing business precondition.

example.error: Lead cannot transition from NEW to WON.

ExternalServiceUnavailable.description: `ExternalServiceError` - the Python LLM service (or the Gemini embedding  gateway) failed or was unreachable. The upstream message is sanitized;  the caller only sees that the AI service is unavailable.

example.error: AI service is unavailable. Please try again later.

PayloadTooLarge.description: Request body over the 2 MB JSON limit.

UnauthorizedPortal.description: The portal token is missing, malformed, revoked, expired, or bound to a  different proposal.

example.error: Client portal session is invalid or expired.

AuthSessionCreated.description: Account and organization created. Sets `presaleee_access`; the refresh  token is only in the body here.

AuthUserOnly.description: Session established. Both httpOnly cookies are set; no token appears in  the body.

LeadList.description: A page of leads, without the RFP text.

ProposalList.description: A page of proposals, without sheets.

AuditLogList.description: A page of ledger entries, newest first.

SuccessEnvelope.description: The shape every successful JSON response shares.

error.description: Human-readable message. Upstream AI detail is sanitized.

statusCode.description: Repeats the HTTP status inside the body.

PaginatedResult.description: Pagination block used by every list except the dashboard widgets, which  report the returned length instead.

total.description: Rows matching the filter across the whole tenant.

totalPages.description: ceil(total / limit), never zero - an empty result is 1.

HealthProbe.description: Not wrapped in the success envelope.

UserRole.description: The five defined roles. Note that `PRESALE_CONSULTANT`, accepted by the  portal manager lists, is not one of them.

CurrencyCode.description: Three letters, case-insensitive on input and upper-cased on storage.

AuditResultStatus.description: `FAILED` is declared but never written by any code path, so a filter on it  always returns an empty page.

ClientIndustry.description: Display labels, not codes - sending `FINANCIAL_SERVICES` is a `400`.

MeetingStatus.description: `INSPECTED` is only reachable through a successful analysis; `OPEN` is the  only status in which a transcript can be written.

ProposalSheetName.description: The ten standard sheets, in the order they are created. All ten are visible  to a client through the portal; there is no internal-sheet flag.

RateSource.description: Which path produced the line's monthly rate - the value a reviewer needs to  see before trusting a quotation.

DashboardActivityType.description: Only these four exist because the feed is derived from entity timestamps.

PublicAuthUser.description: The token-derived identity shape. No password or hash is ever serialized.

plan.description: Always `FREE` today; the column has no other writer.

RegisterSession.description: Registration signs the caller in immediately - only the access token is also  set as a cookie.

refreshToken.description: Opaque 32-256 character token, returned in the body exactly once and  stored hashed.

MemberDirectoryEntry.description: Directory row. `organizationName` is only present on  `GET /users?allOrganizations=true`; single-organization reads omit it.

contactEmail.description: Free text - not format-validated on write.

country.description: 2-100 characters starting with a letter. A NULL in the database is read  back as `Vietnam`.

RateCard.description: Money columns are rounded to two decimals and capped at 1e9 by  `nonNegativeAmount`.

monthlyRateUsd.description: Derived when absent - daily x 21, else hourly x 8 x 21 (21 billable days  is a domain constant).

roleName.description: Must match an active rate card unless an override is given.

manMonths.description: Must be greater than zero and at most 1200 person-months.

monthlyRateOverride.description: Positive values only - an override of zero is ignored rather than  silently free labour.

PricingLine.description: One priced line of the bill of materials.

ExtractedMetadata.description: Free-form JSON owned by the intake analyzer and read by the proposal  generator. Recognized keys and their shapes are listed here; anything else  is stored verbatim.

discoveryInsights.description: Appended by a successful meeting analysis.

Lead.description: The full lead row, as returned by create, get and patch.

bantScore.description: 0-100. `APPROVED` cannot be reached while this is null.

LeadListItem.description: The list projection of a lead - identical to `Lead` minus `rawRfpContent`  and `bantDetails`, which is what keeps `GET /leads` cheap.

QualificationCriterion.description: One BANT dimension. The four scores must sum to the total.

LeadQualification.description: Validated before it is written: an out-of-range score, an unknown  recommendation or a total that does not match the criteria aborts with  `409` and leaves the lead untouched.

IntakeDraftLead.description: A lead that does not exist yet - every persisted column is null so the UI  cannot accidentally treat it as saved.

missingInformation.description: What the RFP did not answer, phrased as items to ask about.

email.description: Trimmed before validation, so surrounding spaces are fine.

deadline.description: Free text, not a date column.

MeetingGapAnalysis.description: Always an object with three arrays. When nothing has been analyzed it is  three empty arrays, never `{}`.

MeetingAnalysis.description: The raw AI result as stored, `{}` before the first successful analysis.

ProposalSheet.description: `sheetData` is a free-form object whose keys depend on the sheet. The  defaults written on creation all begin with `title`; then Overview adds  `projectName`, `executiveSummary`, `keyObjectives`, `currency`; Scope of  Work `modules`; Architecture & Tech Stack `stack`,  `nonFunctionalRequirements`; Timeline & Milestones `totalWeeks`,  `milestones`; Team & Rate Cards `roles`, `totalEffortManMonths`,  `totalTeamCost`; Pricing & Quotation `currency`, `items`, `subtotal`,  `taxPercentage`, `taxAmount`, `grandTotal`; Assumptions & Dependencies  `items`; Risk Management (RAID) `risks`; SLA & Maintenance `warrantyMonths`,  `warrantyTerms`, `incidentMatrix`; Appendices & Case Studies `caseStudies`.

Proposal.description: The projection without sheets, as returned by list, patch and  submit-review.

leadId.description: Set only through `POST /leads/{leadId}/proposals`; nulled by a lead  delete.

RagSourceLite.description: A citation for AI-generated proposal content.

PortalSessionWithToken.description: The only response in the API that carries a usable portal credential - the  plaintext token exists nowhere else.

accessToken.description: 43-character base64url; present only in this response.

PortalSessionDetail.description: Staff-side session row; no token material at all.

PortalMaterial.description: The client-facing projection - no `isShared` and no `createdBy`, which is  also what `POST /proposals/{proposalId}/portal-materials` returns.

fileUrl.description: Always an `https://` URL; nothing is uploaded here.

authorEmail.description: Taken from the session, never from the request body.

ClientPortalSheet.description: Sheet content without the internal identifiers, so a client cannot infer  the row ids used by staff routes.

ClientPortalProposal.description: The client view. All ten sheets are exposed, internal ones included - a  recorded finding.

excerpt.description: First 1800 characters of the sheet's JSON.

KnowledgeDocument.description: Metadata only - there is no `content` column on `knowledge_docs`, so the  document body is not readable back from this row.

category.description: Free text; `GENERAL` when ingest omits it.

domain.description: Free text; `GENERAL` when ingest omits it.

fileType.description: Always `TEXT` - the only supported ingest kind.

DocumentChunk.description: A retrieval hit. `embedding` is deliberately never serialized.

chunkIndex.description: Always 0 today - the retrieval SQL does not select `chunk_index`, so the  position within the document is lost.

label.description: Numbered marker used in the answer text, for example `[1]`.

activeLeads.description: Every status except WON, LOST and REJECTED.

amount.description: A null `total_cost` is summed as zero; REJECTED proposals are excluded.

DashboardPipelineStage.description: `count` is the number of leads in the stage, counted on its own;  `estimatedValueByCurrency` is the joined proposal money per currency. These  were once fed from the same grouped query, which made a multi-currency stage  report one currency's count.

pipeline.description: Always nine entries, in pipeline order.

DashboardLead.description: A widget projection - enough for a card, and deliberately not the full lead  (no RFP text, no client id).

id.description: Synthetic key `<entityId>:created` or `<entityId>:updated`, so at most  two events per entity can ever exist.

DashboardListMeta.description: Warning - `total` is the length of the returned array, not the tenant-wide  count, unlike every other list in this API.

AuditLogEntry.description: Immutable read model: there is no route to create, update or delete a row,  and immutability currently rests on that absence rather than on database  triggers. `ip_address` is stored but never returned.

actorName.description: `users.full_name` via LEFT JOIN, so a removed actor is null.

payload.description: Before/after detail. A stored value that is not a JSON object becomes  `{}`.

organizationDomain.description: `null`, an empty string or an absent key all store NULL.

password.description: Non-empty only - the 12-character policy applies when setting, not when signing in.

currentPassword.description: Verified against the stored hash; wrong is `401`.

proposalId.description: When present and `apply` is not false, the computed total is written to  this proposal.

apply.description: Defaults to true when `proposalId` is given. `apply=true` without a  `proposalId` is a `400`.

extractedMetadata.description: Must be a JSON object; defaults to `{}`.

UpdateLeadRequest.description: `status` is deliberately not accepted here; the state machine lives on  `PATCH /leads/{id}/status`.

meetingDate.description: Any value `new Date()` can parse; defaults to the moment of the call.  Unparsable is `400`.

totalCost.description: Seeded from the Pricing sheet's `grandTotal` when omitted.

estimatedTimelineWeeks.description: Seeded from the Timeline sheet's `totalWeeks` when omitted.

initialSheets.description: Names must be standard, no duplicates, `sheetOrder` must match the  standard order and `sheetData` must be a non-array object. When omitted  all ten blank sheets are created.

UpdateProposalRequest.description: Metadata keys and `status` are mutually exclusive in one request, and  metadata requires the proposal to still be DRAFT.

sheetNames.description: Omit to generate all ten sheets.

fileUrl.description: HTTP is refused; the URL must be https.

content.description: Split into roughly 400-word chunks with a 50-word overlap; the text  itself is only kept inside the chunk rows.

category.description: Free text. An empty string is rejected; omit it for `GENERAL`.

domain.description: Free text. An empty string is rejected; omit it for `GENERAL`.

topK.description: 1-20 here, while `POST /knowledge/ask` caps the same idea at 1-10.
